public_rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and the searched record supplies no decisive event meeting the causal and comparative criteria. [GE's announcement](https://www.ge.com/news/press-releases/ge-board-of-directors-approves-spin-off-of-ge-vernova-ge-vernova-and-ge-aerospace-to) documents restructuring plans, not the asserted cause or a technology-sector outcome. [Technology-sector research](https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/articles/are-technology-stocks-cheap-now) reports market weakness alongside earnings strength. Neither establishes uniquely severe, shareholder-caused consequences.
limitations: Shareholder-first governance has no single specified measure.
A stock selloff, isolated restructuring or evidence about GE alone cannot settle the forecast.
The sector evidence does not constitute a complete causal study through the evaluation date.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Shareholder supremacy will uniquely punish the tech industry as it did General Electric.

statement.excerpt: The deep poison of the Shareholder Supremacy — the nihilistic intention of contorting companies to please analysts and investors — is one that will uniquely punish the tech industry, just like it did to General Electric.

from_speaker: contorting companies to please analysts and investors
will uniquely punish the tech industry
just like it did to General Electric
our_interpretation: The forecast concerns sustained deterioration in major technology companies' economic position, comparable to the GE decline invoked in the passage.
Shareholder-first policies must cause the deterioration; their coexistence with a downturn is insufficient.
Uniquely is read as distinctively severe relative to other sectors, not as claiming that only technology can suffer, since GE is itself the comparison.
The GE reference is a historical analogy, not evidence that the technology-sector forecast has occurred.
criteria.support_condition: Broad, sustained GE-like decline or distress-driven restructuring among major technology companies, credibly caused by shareholder-first policies and distinctively severe relative to comparable sectors.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence ruling out the asserted causal and sector-specific consequences. A temporary recovery or successful individual firm would not suffice.

evidence.explanation: GE announced board approval of the separation and its planned continuing identity. This documents restructuring plans, not that shareholder-first policies caused GE's difficulties or will cause similar technology-sector harm.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A sustained technology-sector decline comparable to the GE example, supported by evidence that shareholder-first policies caused it and that comparable sectors suffered distinctly less under an appropriate comparison.
